title: Your own holy days
hookLine: anniversaries, births, deaths, turning points: Smyrna kept its bishop's death day as his birthday
tomorrow: Seneca visited his old house and didn't know his own trees. why?

lines: A DEATH DAY CALLED A BIRTHDAY?
cards: A phone remembers birthdays for you. It has no field for the day someone died, the day you left, the day everything turned. A church in the old city of Smyrna once kept a different kind of calendar.
Their bishop, Polycarp, was an old man when the authorities ordered him to curse Christ. He refused, and he was killed in the stadium.
So why, a letter from that church says, did they plan to keep the day of his death with gladness, and call it a birthday?

teach.b: The letter tells what they did next. They gathered his bones, dearer to them than precious stones, and laid them in a fitting place. And they planned to meet there, in gladness, to keep the birthday of his martyrdom.

Birthday: the day his life was finished and, as they believed, began. From days like this one grew a Christian custom: keeping a saint's feast on the day they died, their birthday into heaven, in Latin dies natalis.
That's why, on the church calendar, a saint's day can be a death day. Inside the tradition, people argued over birthdays.

teach.h: HIS DEATH DAY KEPT AS A BIRTHDAY.
teach.b: The scholar Origen noticed that the only birthday parties he could find in scripture belong to Pharaoh and to Herod, and both ended with someone put to death.
Ecclesiastes seems to lean his way: a good name is better than precious ointment, it says, "and the day of death than the day of one's birth."
The other side has the angel, promising that at John the Baptist's coming "many shall rejoice at his birth." And the church kept that too: John's birth has its own feast. So the calendar holds both.
A death can be kept as a birthday, and a birth can be holy.
What the calendar won't do is let the days that made a life pass by unmarked. Births, deaths, the day you moved, the day you got well: a life has its own feast days, if someone keeps them.

how: The church calendar keeps saints' feasts, often on the day they died, and a few births, like John the Baptist's. Families also keep their own days: anniversaries of a death, a wedding, a birth.

games.q: what does “your own holy days” mean?
o: the days off your job gives you for a rest
the public holidays printed on every wall calendar
the births, deaths and turning points you choose to keep

games.q: two kinds of holy days: tap the pairs.
p: the old bishop who refused to curse Christ
kept his death day as a birthday
found birthday parties only for Pharaoh, Herod
many shall rejoice at his birth

s: a saint's day on the church calendar is often the day the saint died
it's kept as their birthday into heaven, as Smyrna kept Polycarp's.
the church only ever marked deaths, never births
it kept births too: John the Baptist's birth has its own feast.
Smyrna planned to keep Polycarp's day in mourning
the letter says they planned to meet in gladness, for the birthday of his martyrdom.

games.q: Theo says marking a death anniversary is morbid; days should be for birthdays. make the best case for the other side, from Smyrna.
o: Smyrna kept Polycarp's death day with gladness, as a birthday: a finished life, worth gathering for.
death days were kept as warnings, to make people afraid of dying unprepared.
Smyrna marked it only because nobody knew his real birthday.
games.why: The letter calls it the birthday of his martyrdom, kept in gladness. Theo's side has a voice too: the angel's "many shall rejoice at his birth," and John's feast.

practice: Open your calendar, or a blank page. Write down three days that are holy to you: a birth, a death, a turning point. Then give each one its own stretch of the sit, one at a time, in quiet.

wordCard.voice: Your own holy days: the births, deaths and turning points you choose to mark, the way Smyrna marked Polycarp's day.

orig.note: Latin: birthday. The church's word for the day a saint died, born into heaven.

carryVoice: Your line: my days. Smyrna kept a death day as a birthday, and the church kept John's birth too. Day 1641, marked.

sources.ref: The Martyrdom of Polycarp 9-18 (the demand to revile Christ, his death in the stadium; ch. 18: bones dearer than precious stones, the gathering in gladness for 'the birthday of his martyrdom')
